headline: BESQUE is essentially a one-product brand, and that product is losing ground: the Original Magic Body Oil's sales rank has slipped from about 5,400 in July to about 17,000, while the ad spend sits on generic searches where a £50 oil struggles to compete.

points.title: Original Magic Body Oil: act on the sales slide now
points.detail: The body oil family (~£18k/mo, about 77% of revenue) has gone from a Beauty sales rank of ~5,400 in July to ~17,000 now, and is about 2x worse than a year ago, even though reviews keep growing. With one product carrying the brand, that slide is the main risk.
evidence: B0DJH54BLF monthly sales rank (Keepa): Jul 2026 5,393; Aug 8,559; Sep 13,772; Oct 17,010 (Oct 2025: 8,243)
Family ~198 units/mo at £50 (Jungle Scout, parent-level); Keepa shows 100+ bought last month on the single

points.title: Defend the BESQUE brand searches from a lookalike
points.detail: A £9.99 'Magic Firming Body Oil' (3.6★) buys the ad slot on 'besque' searches, and BESQUE runs no ads on its own name or on 'besque magic body oil'. Brand-term ads are cheap and stop shoppers who are looking for you from buying a copy.
evidence: 'besque': lookalike 'Magic Firming Body Oil, Compact Body Oil, Magic Luxury Body Oil…' sponsored at #4, £9.99, 3.6★ (DataForSEO, Amazon UK)
Same product organic #6 on 'besque magic body oil'
No BESQUE sponsored placement on either brand search

points.title: Move ad spend from generic 'body oil' to firming and crepey-skin searches
points.detail: On 'body oil' (27k/mo) BESQUE sits at organic #27 and sponsored #38, against page-one rivals at ~£9.50 and 4.6★, so a £50 oil struggles to convert there. The premium fits shoppers looking for firming results: 'body oil for women' (4.3k/mo, organic #16, no ads), 'firming body oil' (#34) and rival premium firming oils like Nord Body (3.7k/mo).
evidence: body oil: 27,417/mo, organic #27, sponsored #38 (Jungle Scout); page-one median £9.49 and 4.6★ vs BESQUE £50 and 3.9★
body oil for women: 4,276/mo, organic #16, no sponsored rank
firming body oil: 850/mo, organic #34; body oil for crepey skin: 1,105/mo, organic #31 (already sponsored #4)
nord body multi peptide body oil: 3,701/mo, organic #65; cellu overnight firming oil: 3,319/mo, organic #62
Sponsored on 51 terms in total, including 'body care' at ~£2.00 CPC

points.title: Lift the 3.9★ rating before scaling spend
points.detail: With over 1,000 reviews at 3.9★ against a 4.6★ page-one norm, the rating is the brake on a £50 price point. The listing itself is strong (7 videos, A+, 5 detailed bullets), so the work is in the review drivers: what the low-star reviews say, inserts and expectation-setting in the copy.
evidence: Listing: 8 images, 7 videos, A+, 5 bullets averaging 218 characters

points.title: Give the new launches a proper start
points.detail: The Unscented Magic Body Oil (18 reviews) and Luxury Shower Oil (28 reviews) make about £3k a month each. The shower oil already pays for a #15 ad slot on 'shower oil' (11.6k/mo) against established brands. A launch plan with Vine reviews and tighter ads would reduce the reliance on one product.
evidence: shower oil: 11,566/mo; BESQUE sponsored #15, organic #83; ads above from Uriage, L'Occitane, Nuxe, SVR

hero_actions.B0DJH54BLF: Brand-term ads on 'besque' and 'besque magic body oil', then move generic 'body oil' spend to firming and crepey-skin searches.
hero_actions.B0FKC87JSM: Launch support: Vine reviews, plus ads on 'magic luxury body oil' and unscented and sensitive-skin searches.

content_note: The hero listing is well built (8 images, 7 videos, A+, detailed bullets). The constraint is the 3.9★ rating, not the content.
ad_strategy_summary: Defend the brand name first, then shift budget from generic 'body oil' (where a £50 oil competes with £4–17 products) to firming, crepey-skin and premium-competitor searches where the price makes sense.
amc_hypotheses: The body oil offers Subscribe & Save, so repeat buyers are likely a meaningful share of revenue, and keeping them matters while new-customer sales slow.
With a lookalike advertising on the brand name, some shoppers who search 'besque' probably end up buying the £9.99 copy.
amc_questions: How many Magic Body Oil buyers reorder, and how soon?
Is the sales slide coming from fewer new customers, or fewer repeat orders?
Which searches and ad types bring in buyers who later reorder?
How many shoppers who search the brand name buy another product instead?
